key_insight: HEPTv2 is an end-to-end point-transformer that reconstructs charged-particle tracks directly from detector hits without graph building or clustering, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs.
engineering_relevance: This makes real-time track reconstruction more practical for HL-LHC-scale workloads by cutting latency and memory while preserving high tracking efficiency.
method: Locality-aware point encoder uses locality-sensitive hashing in detector coordinate space for efficient local attention.
Sectorized track decoder predicts complete trajectories directly from hits, avoiding auxiliary graph construction and filtering.
Joint encoder-decoder supervision enables end-to-end optimization of the full pipeline.
evidence_signal: On TrackML, HEPTv2 reaches 98.6% double-majority tracking efficiency at a 0.8% fake rate with about 15 ms inference time and 0.4 GB peak memory on an NVIDIA A100.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of detector-coordinate locality and may require careful tuning to maintain efficiency on much larger or differently distributed hit patterns.
paper_title: HEPTv2: End-to-End Efficient Point Transformer for Charged Particle Reconstruction
